# P26.18 — Chunked-commit write path for very-large sources (SOURCES.17)

## Summary

`PgClaimSink.assert_claims` wrapped an entire source's claim sequence in **one**
`self._conn.transaction()`. For `camreg_osm_surveillance` (~1.37M claims) that is
a single ~13h transaction on the `db-f1-micro` Cloud SQL spine; the P26.16 hosted
run (batch-05 exec `nf8jl`) hit the 36h task deadline and rolled the whole thing
back — the source committed **0 claims** while every other P26.16 source landed
(`docs/build/runs/P26.16.md`). This PR makes the write path commit in **bounded
chunks** so a very-large source lands *progressively* and *resumably*, never
all-or-nothing — without ever bending the append-only invariant.

## What changed

- **`db/src/db/claim_sink.py`** — `assert_claims` commits in chunks of a
  configurable `commit_chunk_size` (module default `DEFAULT_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE =
  10_000`), each chunk its own `transaction()`. A claim and **all** its
  prerequisite/evidence inserts stay in one chunk (they run inside a single
  `_insert_claim` call), so a chunk boundary never bisects a claim. Ctor rejects
  `commit_chunk_size < 1`. `SinkReport` counters are instance state, exact across
  boundaries.
- **`connectors/src/connectors/sinks.py`** — `resolve_commit_chunk_size()` +
  `ENV_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE = "SIG_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE"`: explicit flag wins, else the
  env var, else `None` (the sink default applies). Fail-loud on a non-positive /
  non-numeric value.
- **`connectors/src/connectors/runner.py`** — threads `commit_chunk_size` through
  `run_source` → `_run_live` and `run_connector_over_fixture` (PG sink only;
  `None` = default).
- **`connectors/src/connectors/cli.py`**, **`ops/src/ops/cli.py`** — a
  `--commit-chunk-size` flag (default `$SIG_COMMIT_CHUNK_SIZE`) on
  `sig-connectors run` and `sig-ops scheduled-ingest`.
- **`ops/src/ops/scheduled.py`** — `scheduled_ingest` passes `commit_chunk_size`
  to the runner.
- **Tests** — `tests/db/test_claim_sink.py` (+5 cases): idempotent chunked replay,
  single-vs-chunked row parity, interrupted-then-resumed resumability, runtime
  no-UPDATE/DELETE + N-transaction proof, ctor validation.
  `tests/connectors/test_commit_chunk_size.py` (resolver).

## Design decisions

- **Chunking is durability, not speed.** Commits land progressively so a task
  deadline can't roll back the whole source; throughput is unchanged. This makes
  big ingests *resumable* — strictly better than all-or-nothing.
- **Append-only is sacred.** No UPDATE/DELETE added anywhere; content-digest
  `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` idempotency holds across chunk boundaries and across an
  interrupted-then-resumed run (both proven on a real PG18 testcontainer).
- **Additive / back-compat.** `commit_chunk_size` is optional; the default (10k)
  leaves every ordinary source committing in a single chunk — unchanged behaviour.
  Only OSM-scale sources span multiple chunks.
- **Chunk size is config, not code** — read from the env at the composition roots,
  never hard-coded (root/ops AGENTS.md convention).
